name: Vector_3
questiontext:
Let \({\bf v_{1}}\), \({\bf v_2}\), \({\bf v_3}\) be the following vectors:
\[ {\bf v_{1}} = {{CT:0}},\quad {\bf v_{2}} = {{CT:1}},\quad {\bf v_{3}} = {{CT:2}}. \]
Find the values for \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) such that
\[{\bf v_3} = \lambda_1 {\bf v_1} + \lambda_2 {\bf v_2} .\]
If such values do not exist, enter zero for both entries. \(\lambda_1\) = [[input:ans1]] \(\lambda_2\) = [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans1]] [[validation:ans2]]
generalfeedback:
If \[{\bf v_3} = \lambda_1 {\bf v_1} + \lambda_2 {\bf v_2},\] we have 3 equations in 2 unknowns.
For there to be a solution for \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) the vectors \({\bf v_1},{\bf v_2}\) and \({\bf v_3}\) must be linearly dependent.
This requires the determinant of the matrix of vectors to be zero.
The matrix is \[{{CT:3}}\] with a determinant of \( {{CT:4}}\)
Therefore the vectors are not linearly dependent and there is no solution for \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\)
